title: EditPlan
description: B-EDIT's deterministic, machine-executable timeline handed to the renderer (FFmpeg/Remotion). Built from final_script.json's blocks (positioned on the timeline using ACTUAL measured narration timing from tts_manifest.json, not the estimated_duration_sec Agent A guessed) plus asset_inventory.json's beat_coverage allocations. No creative decisions remain for the renderer -- it only executes. Every clip distinguishes TWO timelines: timeline_start_sec/timeline_end_sec (where the clip appears in the FINAL DOCUMENTARY) versus source_start_sec/source_end_sec (which range is taken from the SOURCE asset, video only). A usable_segment recorded during B-DISCOVER is a permitted source RANGE, not an indivisible clip -- B-EDIT may use any subrange of it, or several different subranges across different clips, as long as each stays inside the segment's own start_sec/end_sec.

clips.description: The complete ordered visual timeline, sorted by timeline_start_sec ascending with no overlaps. Prefer fewer, longer, coherent clips over frequent cuts -- there is no 'change image every N seconds' rule; a strong clip may run long if it still supports the narration.

segment_id.description: Video only. References one of the asset's usable_segments[].segment_id from asset_inventory.json. Required for a video clip; absent for a still/document clip.

timeline_start_sec.description: Where this clip starts in the FINAL DOCUMENTARY (e.g. 202.0 = 03:22).

timeline_end_sec.description: Where this clip ends in the FINAL DOCUMENTARY. Must exceed timeline_start_sec.

source_start_sec.description: Video only, required when segment_id is set. Where the used range starts WITHIN THE SOURCE asset. Must fall inside the referenced usable_segment's own [start_sec, end_sec] -- the segment is a permitted range, not a fixed clip; this may be any subrange of it.

source_end_sec.description: Video only, required when segment_id is set. Must exceed source_start_sec and stay inside the referenced usable_segment.

still_treatment.description: Stills/documents only. Deliberately small enum -- not a motion-graphics system. The renderer executes exactly this, it does not choose.
